correctness.rationale: Every finite graph edge gradient yields the exact Lip_0 norm; injectivity of finite ell_infty identifies the absolute constant with the relative one. Duality rewrites the latter as min ||I-P|| over cycle-space retractions. Averaging all within-path coordinate permutations and permutations of p equal paths reduces every optimizer to one real x. Exact complete edge-column norms and monotonicity outside [0,1/p] reduce the problem to the maximum of two affine functions; exhaustive case analysis gives every branch and its boundary. The finite rational and unrestricted LP checks are supplementary only.

value.rationale: The exact absolute projection constants of a natural p+1-path network Banach family are a motivated invariant. The theorem identifies short-path, balanced, and saturating geometries, an explicit finite exceptional-length threshold, and eventual constancy despite indefinitely increasing one path. It goes substantially beyond the known two-edge-path diamond special case, giving an exact infinite three-parameter classification.
